problem: RunState.RegisterKill is not atomic when it throws. It increments Kills first and validates second: after the IsOver early-return it executes `Kills++` and only then calls AddScore(scoreValue), which is where the negative-value guard lives. So RegisterKill(-1) increments Kills, then throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException out of AddScore. The caller sees a failed call and has every reason to assume nothing happened, but the run's kill count has permanently gained one that no enemy died for, while Score correctly gained nothing. The two counters RegisterKill exists to keep in step are left out of step by the very path that was supposed to prevent the change. The thrown exception also names the wrong parameter: it carries paramName "amount" and the message "Score never decreases in this game", which points a reporter at AddScore's parameter for a call the code under test never made, so the bug report starts one frame away from the actual call site. This is reachable, not theoretical: Assets/Unity/GameManager.cs:47 exposes RegisterKill as a public passthrough taking an arbitrary int, so any death handler or enemy configuration that yields a negative score value corrupts Kills and then throws inside a Unity callback, where the exception is logged and swallowed by the engine and the run carries on with an inflated kill count. No WO-0007 criterion covers this. Criterion 6 only requires RegisterKill not to change TickCount or Seed, and criterion 11 preserves the pre-existing contract, which is exactly what this ordering is -- pre-existing. Neither test suite exercises it: Assets/Tests/Core.Tests/RunStateTests.cs tests RejectsNegativeScore through AddScore only, and RunStateVerificationTests.cs does the same at Criterion11_NegativeScoreThrows. No test anywhere calls RegisterKill with a negative argument, so the partial mutation has never been observed.
evidence: Assets/Core/Run/RunState.cs:100-109 -- RegisterKill increments Kills at line 107 before delegating validation to AddScore at line 108; AddScore's guard at lines 86-90 then throws with the Kills increment already applied
Assets/Core/Run/RunState.cs:88-89 -- the exception surfaced from a RegisterKill call carries `nameof(amount)`, naming AddScore's parameter rather than RegisterKill's scoreValue

Assets/Unity/GameManager.cs:47 -- `public void RegisterKill(int scoreValue) => Run.RegisterKill(scoreValue);` passes an unvalidated int straight through from the shell, making the negative path reachable from gameplay code

Assets/Tests/Core.Tests/RunStateTests.cs:62-67 (RejectsNegativeScore) and Assets/Tests/Core.Tests/RunStateVerificationTests.cs:469-474 (Criterion11_NegativeScoreThrows) -- both cover the negative path only through AddScore; neither suite calls RegisterKill with a negative value

Studio/orders/open/WO-0007.json acceptance criteria 6 and 11 -- criterion 6 constrains RegisterKill only with respect to TickCount and Seed, and criterion 11 freezes the pre-existing contract, so this ordering is outside the twelve criteria rather than a failure against them
proposedWork: A follow-up L3 work order to engineering, scoped to Assets/Core/Run/** and Assets/Tests/Core.Tests/**, making RegisterKill validate before it mutates: move the negative check to the top of RegisterKill, ahead of both the IsOver early-return's side effects and the Kills increment, and throw ArgumentOutOfRangeException with nameof(scoreValue) so the exception names the parameter the caller actually supplied. The existing delegation to AddScore stays, so a valid call behaves identically and Score and Kills still move together. The work order should also state the general invariant the fix restores, because it will apply to every future mutator on this type: a RunState method that throws must leave the object exactly as it found it. Ship it with a regression test that calls RegisterKill(-1) on a fresh run, asserts ArgumentOutOfRangeException, and then asserts Kills is still zero and Score is still zero -- the Kills assertion fails today and passes after the change -- plus a test asserting the exception's ParamName is "scoreValue".
expectedBenefit: Restores fail-atomicity to the one RunState method that mutates two fields, so a rejected kill cannot inflate the kill count. Because the exception escapes into a Unity callback where the engine logs and continues, the corrupted count would otherwise survive to the end of the run and into whatever score is reported, with the only visible trace being a console line nobody correlates. Also fixes a misdirecting paramName that would send a defect report to the wrong method.
